Subject: Renewal coming up — mid-contract capacity bump and safety net ask

Hi Marcus,

Our renewal window is coming up for Q2 and we've had a heavier-than-expected burst in November/early December. We're looking to do two things before the contract anniversary:

1) Add ~40% additional committed capacity (effective immediately / prorated through the next renewal).
2) Get a short-term burst safety net (credits or a voucher pool) to cover 6 weeks of peak in case our December pattern repeats while we onboard a new model.

Can Redwood provide a pricing approach that avoids a full calendar-year repricing? Our procurement team would prefer pro-rated top-up + a co-term to the existing renewal date if possible. Also include any available short-term credits we could use for bursts.

I've attached our usage export for November so you can see the spike (mosaic-usage-nov.pdf). If you can send an outline of options and a ballpark delta to our current ARR, procurement and I can review and get legal briefed.

Thanks,
Sarah Jensen
VP, Operations — Mosaic Health

--

Hi Sarah — thanks for the context and the usage export. Appreciate the visibility.

Quick summary of feasible paths from our side (high level):

Option A — Prorated Top-up + Co-term (recommended)
- Add 40% committed capacity today, charged pro-rata to your next renewal date (no forced 12-month min on the top-up).
- Apply a one-time uplift of ~10% on the prorated portion (since we reserve additional GPU headroom).
- Co-term the added capacity to your existing renewal date so you only reconcile once.

Option B — Voucher-based Burst Safety Net + Lower Uplift
- Keep committed capacity unchanged, issue a 6-week burst voucher pool that covers your typical peak token volume.
- Voucher is priced as a one-time fee (~6% of the annualized uplift we'd quote for a 40% add).

Option C — Blended: 20% committed top-up + 6-week voucher for the rest.

I want to make this simple: if procurement wants one invoice and one co-term, Option A gets you predictable billing and the lowest operational overhead. Option B preserves flexibility but is slightly more expensive per-peak token.

Cc-ing Kimberly to weigh in on discounting/approval path and procurement next steps. If you want, I can put together a short formal proposal (with pro-rated math and a sample amendment) — give me a target renewal date you want co-term'd to and I'll return a PDF with figures.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin

Kimberly / Ben — forwarding Mosaic's ask. Key points below and my suggested commercial approach.

- Customer: Mosaic Health (existing annual renewal in 2027-06). They want +40% capacity now, co-term to their 2027-06 renewal, and a 6-week burst safety net.
- Usage spike looks legit (attached).

My suggestion for approval:
- Offer a blended path: 30% immediate committed top-up (prorated), plus a 6-week voucher pool for peak (voucher priced at ~4.5% of the annualized uplift).
- Apply a limited one-time concession: waive the standard 12% uplift on the proration and apply a 9% uplift instead (gives ~3% concession vs baseline).
- Include an SLA addendum for burst routing priority (no change to existing SLA, just escalation/priority routing for a 6-week window).

If we do full 40% committed top-up the discount needs to be tighter; the blended approach keeps runway for upsell and avoids re-architecting their billing. Would appreciate quick sign-off so I can get a formal amendment over to procurement/legal before Friday.

Thanks — Marcus
